paper.title_en: Scalable vacuum manifold system for proportional counters to extend GRAPES-3 large-area muon detectors
paper.abstract_en: The expansion of the GRAPES-3 muon telescope to double its sensitive area required large-scale refurbishment of thousands of legacy proportional counters originally deployed in the Kolar Gold Field (KGF) experiment. To enable efficient and reproducible detector preparation, a series of high-performance vacuum manifold systems was developed for evacuation, leak testing, and gas filling under high-throughput conditions. The system evolved over a decade from early asymmetric prototypes to a third-generation symmetric (7＋7 port) configuration. Constructed from SS316 stainless steel to minimize outgassing and ensure corrosion resistance, the optimized 1250 mm manifold achieved an ultimate vacuum of <math altimg="si20.svg" display="inline" id="d1e398"><mrow><mn>3.6</mn><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">×</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> mbar. Performance characterization, including stress testing under simulated power failures, demonstrated mechanical robustness and rapid recovery. The system enables preparation of up to 10 detectors per day while maintaining gas purity and operational stability. This design provides a robust, portable, and cost-effective framework for large-scale preparation of gaseous detectors in modern particle physics experiments.
